orig.credit: Anonymous; the Latin text of the Psalteriolum Cantionum Catholicarum (1710), as quoted in Wikipedia's article

stanzas: deprived of the Son of God.
will be born for you, Israel.
Come, O little rod of Jesse!
From the enemy's claw your own,
from the cave of Tartarus your own
lead out, and from the pit of the abyss.
drive away the mists of night
and the dreadful darkness of night.
make safe the road of those above,
and close the ways of those below.
who to the people on Sinai
gave the law from the summit,

notes: 3.2-3.4: one sentence: 'lead your own out from the enemy's claw, from the cave of Tartarus, and from the pit of the abyss'; 'Ex hostis tuos ungula' is translated as printed.
4.1: 'Oriens', the rising (sun), the dawn; also rendered 'Dayspring'.
5.3-5.4: 'superum' and 'inferum' are genitive plurals: the road of those above (heaven) and the ways of those below (the underworld).
6.1: Adonai, Hebrew 'Lord', kept as a name.
